concern_details.detail: How do these components interact during user registration?
concern_details.why: The participants and the main call chain (form -> LibraryFacade.register -> UserManager.register -> UserRegistry -> PersistenceManager -> DB, factory creation, save) match the code, and the success path is right. The failure paths are wrong or missing, though, and an integration tester needs them most. (a) UserManager.validate/validateStudent/validateLibrarian (UserManager.java:67-75) throw IllegalArgumentException before the registry is called. The view puts its single 'alt invalid' after the registry lookup, which suggests a DB query always runs before any rejection. (b) The duplicate check is two lookups in order, each with its own exception: institutionalEmailExists (findFirstByFields on User) throws 'Email is already associated...' (UserManager.java:77-79), and only then findStudentByStudentNumber or findLibrarianByCode, chosen by role, throws 'Identifier is already in use' (81-86). The view merges both into one query. (c) A failed save (PersistenceManager.save catches the exception, rolls back and returns false; UserManager.java:92-95 then throws RuntimeException) is left out, but Registration.java catches RuntimeException and shows it. (d) The form's 'Complete all fields' early return (Registration.java:126-130) is drawn as a self-call with no outcome.

level_why: Eight lifelines at component granularity (form, facade, manager, registry, factories, persistence, DB) fits 'balanced' for an integration tester: each lifeline is an integration boundary they can stub or assert on. Field-level validations are rightly collapsed into one self-call. The fixes below change the existing interactions or add alt operands; they add no new lifelines, so the view stays at the given level.
unsupported: The 'alt invalid' operand comes after 'check email and identifier unused', so the code's validation failures (UserManager.validate*, lines 67-75) appear to happen after a registry/DB lookup. In the code they are thrown before any registry call.

'registry -> persistence : find first by field' / 'persistence -> db : query' is drawn as one lookup. The code makes two separate lookups in order (email on User, then studentNumber on Student or internalIdentifierCode on Librarian, UserRegistry.java:37-60), and the second runs only if the first finds nothing.

The note says the REST path is 'identical' from the facade onwards. That holds for the calls, but AuthenticationController.register (SpringBoot/AuthenticationController.java:22-30) has no exception handling, so on REST the error outcome is an unhandled exception and an HTTP error, not a shown message. The note should say so.
missing: The validation failure exits before any registry access (UserManager.java:67-75 -> IllegalArgumentException -> form showError).
Separate outcomes for duplicate email (line 77-79) and duplicate identifier (lines 81-86), checked in that order, with the identifier lookup depending on role.
The save-failure path: PersistenceManager.save returns false after rollback, and UserManager throws RuntimeException('Server error...') (UserManager.java:92-95), which the form shows as an error.
The form's own 'Complete all fields' rejection (Registration.java:126-130), where no facade call is made.
uml: One 'alt' with guards [invalid] / [new account] cannot represent the three exit points in the code. Use guarded operands in the order the code runs them, e.g. [fields invalid], [email in use], [identifier in use], [save failed], [else], or put each early exit in its own 'opt'/'break' fragment at the point where it is thrown.

The exception return 'manager --> facade : IllegalArgumentException' leaves manager's activation open in that operand; the activation only ends in the other operand. Each operand's return should end the activation, or use a 'break' fragment.

'User factories' is one lifeline standing for two classes that are instantiated with 'new' (UserManager.java:89). Model it as a create message to a 'factory : UserFactory' lifeline (StudentFactory or LibrarianFactory by role), or name the lifeline by the UserFactory interface.

'persistence -> db : query' and 'persistence -> db : insert' are synchronous calls with no reply. Add the replies (rows / insert result) or draw them as asynchronous signals so the message kinds are consistent.
fixes: Move field validation into its own early-exit fragment before any registry call: manager -> manager : validate fields for role; [invalid] IllegalArgumentException -> facade -> form -> show error.

Split the duplicate check into two ordered lookups, each with its own exit: institutionalEmailExists (query User by email) -> [in use] 'Email already associated'; then, by role, findStudentByStudentNumber or findLibrarianByCode -> [in use] 'Identifier already in use'.
Add the save-failure operand: persistence save returns false (rollback) -> registry false -> manager throws RuntimeException 'Server error' -> form shows error.
Show the form's 'Complete all fields' guard as an opt/alt where no facade call is made, so the tester can see which errors never reach the backend.

Correct the REST note to say that exceptions are not handled in AuthenticationController, so REST clients receive an HTTP error, not a message; also fix the factory lifeline/create message and the missing DB replies.
